The Recipe from Grandma: 一道传了三代人的家庭菜谱。
In Lily's family, there is a small old book in the kitchen. It is a recipe book, and the first page was written by Lily's great-grandmother in 1958. Now the book is in Grandma's hands.

The most famous recipe in the book is for apple pie. Every family celebration needs one: birthdays, Christmas, and even the day somebody passes an exam. The rules are strict — the apples must be a special kind from the hill garden, and the pie must stay in the oven for exactly forty-five minutes.

Last weekend, Grandma decided it was time to teach Lily. They worked together all afternoon. Grandma showed her how to mix the butter and flour with fingers, how to fold the dough, and how to arrange the apple pieces 'like flower petals', as the old recipe says.

When the pie came out of the oven, its smell filled the whole house. 'One day, this book will be yours,' Grandma said. Lily understood then: the little book was not really about food. It was about time, love, and a family's story, passed from hand to hand.
